executiveSummary: GM0823's official 2025 identity, contained reference point, 19,536-resident control, fifteen neighbourhoods, two BAG places, twenty BRT settlements and four logical road-border links are coherent, and all ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Oirschot is inland high-sand and beekdal territory: the Groote and Kleine Beerze meet near Baest to form the Beerze, local storage, groundwater, rainwater, sewers, surface water and the Wilhelminakanaal have distinct pathways, and drought and wet-period peak attenuation coexist. The canonical major-river preset instead assigns an exact 1.037729 m depth through T+72, 3,272 to 3,794 affected residents and 125,211 to 504,954 person-hours without a selected Rhine, Meuse or IJssel source or a Beerze/canal hydraulic event. The direct North Sea coastal result of zero depth is reasonable only for that narrowly named source and does not establish safety from local water. Spatial allocation is not mechanism-based: eight active single-hazard families share the same complete neighbourhood order. A controlled ignition in the 2,013 ha Zuid-Oirschotse Heide neighbourhood ranks that source first, but moving the ignition to Westelbeers leaves Westelbeers tenth and Zuid-Oirschotse Heide first. The canonical wildfire reports smoke 0.244881 and nobody affected despite official recognition that regional forest/heath fire can threaten recreation, military functions, A58/provincial roads, power infrastructure and people through smoke and limited access. Dynamic exposure is material but absent: Defensie identifies Oirschot as its largest barracks with about 3,500 workers, while municipal evidence records nature-linked camping/recreation and the airport risk profile describes millions of annual passengers at the external Eindhoven civil/military airport. None is incident-time occupancy, and none enters the resident denominator. The A58 is one physical east-west corridor represented as three series/junction edges; its Wilhelminakanaal bridge has a current precautionary support structure. N395 crosses Middelbeers and Oostelbeers; A2 and Eindhoven Airport are external dependencies rather than direct GM0823 edges/assets. Acute hospital care is external in Eindhoven, Veldhoven or Tilburg. Public context supplies 111 partial water assets, one Enexis capacity-planning sample, provider territories, 59 antenna sites, ten education locations and 42 transit stop areas but no contained Waterinfo, fixed KNMI, RIVM air/acute-care, NDW or seismic record. These data do not supply live topology, occupancy, staffing, stock, backup, outage, passability or restoration. Exact first-72-hour hazard, service and recovery values must remain visibly synthetic or Unknown until selected event forcing, dynamic population, physical dependencies and confirmed actor/resource actions are bound; NoData is never zero, safe, open or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0823 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0823 as Oirschot in Noord-Brabant and Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Zuidoost, with 19,536 residents, density 192/km², 25.0% aged 65 or older and 2,445 one-person households. The reference point [5.297676632792757,51.494675285689844] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Fifteen neighbourhoods in four districts sum to 19,535 residents, one below the municipal control (-0.005%); households total 8,265 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 4,890. Deterministic allocation adds one without rewriting published observations.

Oirschot and Oost West en Middelbeers are the two BAG places. Twenty BRT settlements comprise twelve buurtschappen, one deelkern, three gehuchten and four woonkernen; no BAG place centre falls outside the generalized boundary.
Average home value is null in two neighbourhoods; district-heating and public-charging fields are null in all fifteen. Null remains NoData, not numeric zero or infrastructure absence.

Oirschot-Centrum has 4,470 published residents and De Notel 3,750, while sparse Zuid-Oirschotse Heide covers 2,013 ha with 1,320 residents and Oostelbeers' dispersed area covers 2,189 ha with 670; population weighting cannot replace fuel, hydrology, access or transient occupancy.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Climate-resilient water, Beerze system and local storage context
evidenceSources.edition: Authority project and municipal policy/context pages inspected 3 September 2026; project/policy evidence, not an incident observation or hydraulic forecast; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: De Dommel's Kleine Beerze project covers 6.7 km between Middelbeers and Vessem, reports that parts can fall dry, and uses meandering plus 51 ha of natural storage to retain water, replenish groundwater and attenuate wet-period peaks.
The authority states the Beerze is formed near Landgoed Baest where Groote and Kleine Beerze meet. This is a local catchment pathway, not proof of direct Rhine, Meuse or IJssel inundation.

Municipal landscape evidence identifies temporary water nuisance mainly in parts of beekdalen, while southern conifer forest/heath and some farmland are especially drought-sensitive. The challenges are too wet, too dry and too warm, not one generic flood scalar.

The municipality's Gijzelaar project north of Oirschot targets approximately 13,500 m³ of rainwater storage to reduce sewer overload and support groundwater. Heistraat plans separate stormwater drainage and infiltration, demonstrating urban drainage assets and projects whose live performance is not supplied.

At audit time De Dommel's 2026 material records a seasonal abstraction ban for drought-sensitive Beerze/Reusel waters and emergency support water for parts of the Beerze. This is timestamped regional/current management context, not a local drinking-water outage or automatic scenario forcing.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028
evidenceSources.edition: Public 2025–2028 regional risk-profile document; official scenario/planning evidence, not a current incident, perimeter, inventory or resource state; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The profile says regional nature-fire behavior depends on biomass, fuel availability, rainfall, humidity, temperature, wind, ignition, accessibility and extinguishing water. Nature areas are interwoven with residents, care, recreation and military uses, while A2, A58, A67 and provincial roads can be vulnerable.

It describes smoke and limited access, evacuation and injuries as possible impacts and warns that power lines/transformer infrastructure in nature areas can create larger cascading outages. These regional mechanisms need a selected local source and footprint.

For drinking water it identifies Brabant Water, distinguishes quantity, quality, transport-line, production, cyber and service incidents, and cites a past Oirschot pressure-area transport-line leak causing water nuisance. Regional design redundancy and ten-day self-sufficiency are planning standards, not proof of a selected asset's live state.

If safe drinking water is unavailable for more than 24 hours, the profile describes at least three litres per person per day emergency drinking water, supplied by Brabant Water and distributed by municipalities. This is a conditional operational requirement, not evidence that sites, staff, vehicles or stock are already activated.

Eindhoven airfield supports both military operations and civilian Eindhoven Airport use; the profile reports about 6.8 million annual passenger journeys and about 5,000 military flights and distinguishes airport zone 1 from off-airport response. The airport is outside GM0823; annual regional traffic is not Oirschot incident-time exposure.

The profile covers stationary and road hazardous-material incidents, whose consequence depends on substance, quantity, weather and response. It does not provide a current complete, safe-to-publish GM0823 inventory or incident plume.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Legerplaats Oirschot and Oirschotse Heide public planning context
evidenceSources.edition: Official December 2024 public briefing and 2025 draft National Programme Space for Defence inspected 3 September 2026; planning/context evidence, not an incident roster, asset topology or operational status; Dutch central-government copyright/reuse conditions apply
supports: Defensie describes Oirschot as the Netherlands' largest barracks, with about 3,500 workers, home base of 13 Light Brigade, a military-driving training facility and the large Oirschotse Heide exercise area.

The 2025 draft national programme proposes expansion of the exercise area and environmental space for growing barracks activity; that proposal is planning evidence and must not be treated as already built or occupied.

Workers, trainees, visitors, vehicles and exercises can materially alter daytime population, ignition/access conditions and logistical demand, but no public source inspected supplies a current roster, on-base occupancy, exercise schedule, hazardous inventory, water stock, backup power or response commitment.

Sensitive/security-relevant topology or inventories should remain governed and Unknown in the public simulator; the model should use a Defensie liaison and confirmed aggregate operational effects when an incident warrants it.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — A58 bridge over Wilhelminakanaal and N395 corridor context
evidenceSources.edition: Current RWS project page and 2026 notices plus provincial N395 project material inspected 3 September 2026; infrastructure/works context, not incident-time traffic or passability; Dutch central/provincial reuse conditions apply
supports: RWS says the A58 bridge at Oirschot over the Wilhelminakanaal is safe for current use with a precautionary support structure installed in early 2026; complete replacement is planned by 2030. Current safety is not a T0–T+72 guarantee under an incident.

A58 connects Eindhoven, Tilburg and farther west. The graph's three GM0823 A58 municipality links share physical ID NWB-road-58 and are series/junction views of one physical corridor, not three additive capacities.

The provincial N395 runs about 13 km between Oirschot and Hilvarenbeek and crosses Middelbeers and Oostelbeers. It is a distinct rural/village corridor whose local junctions, bridge/culvert constraints and live traffic are not encoded by one border edge.

A2 is not a direct GM0823 edge in the generated graph; it is an external alternative/dependency reached through Best/Eindhoven and cannot be presented as locally available without route and incident state.
NWB nominal capacities are logical modelling proxies, not measured vehicles per hour, emergency-lane access, closure, smoke visibility, hazmat isolation, bridge load or evacuation throughput.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Zuidoost / Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regionaal Crisisplan 2024–2027 and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Regional crisis plan 2024–2027 plus RIVM acute-care public dataset version 1.1 with 2025 reported figures, deployment snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026; doctrine/register context, not a live resource commitment; plan licence not stated, RIVM data CC0
supports: The plan separates general-chain population decisions such as evacuation from functional-chain decisions for electricity, food safety and other sectors and requires network cooperation and current information.

CoPI addresses place-bound acute incidents; ROT handles non-place-bound effects, partner connection, longer-term effects and recovery. A Defensie liaison is listed for ROT, but a listed role is not proof of activation, staffing or a delivered action.

Recovery preparation starts during response. Bevolkingszorg initiates a multidisciplinary handover document with remaining subjects, actions and owners; formal doctrine does not establish that a local action has occurred or succeeded.

No RIVM acute-care location is contained in GM0823. From the municipal reference point, the registered 24/7 emergency departments are approximately 12.4 km straight-line at Catharina Eindhoven, 13.0 km at Máxima Veldhoven and 14.3 km at ETZ Tilburg; straight-line distance is not route time, capacity or acceptance.
Hospital access, ambulance crews, patient distribution, generator/fuel status, beds, staff and acceptance remain Unknown until incident-valid confirmation.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Landschapskwaliteitsplan and recreational/transient context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal landscape plan published 2021 and current tourism-tax page inspected 3 September 2026; strategic/historic context, not a current occupancy feed; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The plan maps nature-linked overnight recreation mainly in the municipality's west, two recreational axes along Eindhoven–Oirschot and the Beerze valley, eight named larger holiday/camping sites and multiple visitor gateways, while explicitly saying its accommodation map is incomplete.

Current municipal tax rules confirm paid overnight stays by non-residents and distinguish regular, mobile/static camping and group accommodation. Rates and establishment examples do not reveal current people present.
Nature, camping, cycle/walking routes, historic Oirschot centre and events can create strongly time- and weather-dependent exposure in sparse administrative areas.
No inspected governed public source supplies current guests, campers, day visitors, event attendees or hospitality workers per neighbourhood at T0–T+72; all remain Unknown rather than zero.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / RDI / DUO / RIVM / KNMI / Rijkswaterstaat / NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Partial water, utility, telecom, education, care, weather and traffic context
evidenceSources.edition: HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026, CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness; other deployment snapshots queried/retrieved 2–3 September 2026 under source-specific editions/licences; provider point records dated September–December 2025
supports: Full-resolution containment assigns 111 HWH objects: five sewer pumps, two surface-water pumps and 104 weirs. Four sewer-pump and both surface-water-pump records have non-null capacity numbers, but capacity units/connectivity/telemetry are not established here and every weir capacity is null.

One 5689AA planning sample maps to Enexis area BT Best and reports large-user withdrawal/injection capacity, queues, 19 projects and earliest project year 2026. It is planning context, not live local load, outage, reserve or restoration.

At the municipal reference point Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting polygons identify Enexis for power/gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and Ziggo for media; drainage returns no polygon. A point territory lookup is not boundary-wide topology, connectivity, quality, coverage, outage or restoration, and the empty drainage result is Unknown.
RDI assigns 59 sites and DUO ten education locations. Registers do not establish telecom coverage/backhaul/power, school occupancy, shelter designation, staff, supplies or accessibility.

Zero contained Waterinfo observation/forecast, fixed KNMI observation/warning, RIVM PM2.5/acute-care, government-service, NDW-situation and recent seismic points are scoped NoData, never normal conditions, open routes, available service or safety.

The reference point and both BAG place centres lie inside the generalized 2025 geometry.
Administrative edition, planning context, timestamped status, official scenario and synthetic exercise time remain distinct.

Zuid-Oirschotse Heide and dispersed Oostelbeers each exceed 2,000 ha; low density does not imply low fire, visitor, military or access exposure.
Use full-resolution elevation, catchments, water controls, land cover/fuels and current event geometry rather than neighbourhood centroids.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic ledgers reconcile, but local causal provenance does not support exact hazard, people or service values.
notes: Hazard/service contribution sums and counterfactual records remain inspectable.

Canonical wildfire T+24 reports flame zero, smoke 0.244881, zero affected and 22,643 person-hours despite no selected local source; a controlled Zuid-Oirschotse Heide source yields 1,473 affected but remains seed-shaped.
Earthquake has zero local motion, severity and affected residents but 1,478 person-hours at T+24 and 2,543 at T+72; label this as synthetic indirect network effect, not local earthquake damage.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 clearance, persistence and service changes are not driven by confirmed Oirschot actions or resources.
notes: Pluvial depth/affected change 0.312664/505 to 0/0 while burden grows 63,219 to 135,655 without rain, sewer, storage, infiltration, pump or clearance action.
Wildfire smoke/affected change 0.244881/0 to 0/0 while burden grows 22,643 to 65,384 without perimeter, suppression, access, evacuation or re-entry evidence.
Compound depth persists at 0.528693 while affected rises 5,550 to 6,091 and burden grows 187,285 to 762,012; no actor/resource causes that trajectory.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, containment, regional membership and resident reconciliation are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 plus audit:context verify GM0823/Oirschot/Noord-Brabant/VRBZO, both BAG place centres, the contained reference point and a one-resident (-0.005%) rounding difference reconciled deterministically.
findings.action: Retain the 2025 edition, exact nulls, deterministic reconciliation and separate BAG/BRT semantics.

findings.summary: The canonical major-river preset asserts unsupported persistent inundation in inland Oirschot.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 reports depth 1.037729 and severity 0.327088 with affected 3,272→3,794 and burden 125,211→504,954. E02 establishes Beerze, groundwater, storage and local water management, not a selected direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel event.
findings.action: Suppress direct canonical major-river consequence for GM0823; preserve separately selected Beerze/Kleine Beerze, Wilhelminakanaal, groundwater, drainage and indirect supply pathways as Unknown until authority hydraulic evidence is bound.

findings.summary: Direct North Sea coastal zero is plausible only with explicit source scope.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports zero depth/affected but wind 19.698272 m/s and 21,956 person-hours. E02 establishes local inland water pathways; no coast directly borders GM0823.
findings.action: Retain direct North Sea inundation zero only with source label and not-applicable rationale; do not let it suppress local beekdal, canal, groundwater, rain, drainage or indirect logistics Unknowns.

findings.summary: Generic flood depth collapses urban rain, Beerze peaks, groundwater, sewer/storage and drought.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 has rain zero, depth 0.312664 and 505 affected; severe storm retains 0.475989 m after rain/wind fall to zero. E02 documents beekdal nuisance, dry high sands, separate drainage/infiltration and 13,500 m³ planned storage.
findings.action: Bind event rain and groundwater to AHN/BGT, soils, Beerze subcatchments, Wilhelminakanaal interfaces, sewers/pumps/storage/outfalls and current initial/control state; keep drought, drinking water, wastewater and inundation distinct.

findings.summary: Wildfire exposure is source-insensitive and omits recreation, military and access mechanisms.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 identify heath/forest, military/recreational use, smoke, road, power, access and extinguishing-water mechanisms. Canonical wildfire has smoke 0.244881 and zero affected; controlled Westelbeers ignition affects 1,356 yet ranks its source tenth, below Zuid-Oirschotse Heide.
findings.action: Use eligible fuels/moisture, source/perimeter, wind/plume, dynamic occupancy, escape/access, water and suppression inputs; require source/adjacent consequences before unrelated areas and preserve absent live occupancy as Unknown.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active single hazards reuse one exact neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank the same first five and complete ordering. Moving a wildfire source to Westelbeers leaves that source tenth.
findings.action: Replace shared seeded local severity with mechanism-specific hydraulic, groundwater, rain, wind, heat, fuel/fire, plume and cyber surfaces; add source-containment and cross-hazard rank-divergence tests.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure omits barracks/work, recreation and external airport-related transients.
findings.evidence: E04 reports about 3,500 Oirschot barracks workers; E07 records incomplete nature-linked camping/recreation supply; E03 reports large annual civil/military airport flows outside GM0823. Model exposure is capped at 19,536 residents.
findings.action: Add timestamped workers/trainees, guests, day visitors, event/airport-related travellers and responders as separate, non-double-counted cohorts with source and uncertainty; never convert annual flows, sites or jobs into live occupancy.

findings.summary: A58 series duplication, bridge/canal, N395 village access and external acute care are not operationally represented.
findings.evidence: E05 shows one physical A58 corridor, the supported Wilhelminakanaal bridge and N395 through Middelbeers/Oostelbeers. E06 places 24/7 emergency care outside GM0823. The graph has no structure, rural route, live traffic, transit, ambulance or hospital-acceptance state.
findings.action: Model each physical corridor/structure once with direction and issue/valid state; route evacuation, mutual aid, supply and care with congestion, vehicles/crews and destination acceptance, otherwise Unknown.

findings.summary: Aviation, defence and hazardous-material context is either absent or risks being generalized without a selected event.
findings.evidence: E03 distinguishes Eindhoven Airport/Vliegbasis zone and off-airport response and says hazmat impact depends on substance, quantity, weather and response; E04 confirms a major Oirschot defence site. None supplies a current Oirschot incident, zone footprint, plume, roster or safe public inventory.
findings.action: Do not force airport/hazmat impact by proximity; when selected, bind a confirmed location/zone, material/aircraft class, weather/plume, affected people, access and airport/Defensie/operator actions with security-aware aggregation.

findings.summary: Partial water assets and provider/planning context cannot calibrate exact eight-service availability.
findings.evidence: E08 exposes 111 water objects, Enexis/Brabant Water/Ziggo responsibility, one capacity-planning sample, antennas and schools, but not connected networks, live load/flow/pressure/quality, backup, stock, crews or restoration. E03 resilience requirements are standards, not event state.
findings.action: Label percentages synthetic; integrate authorised timestamped aggregate operations and authority-reviewed hydrology only, preserving partial registers, sensitive topology, null capacity and no-match as Unknown.

findings.summary: Absent local observations and mixed evidence classes require explicit coverage and time semantics.
findings.evidence: E08 has zero contained Waterinfo, fixed KNMI, RIVM air/care, NDW and seismic points; E02/E03 include current regional status, policy, past incident and official scenarios. Absence is not zero water/weather/fire/traffic/service or safety.
findings.action: Display publisher/version/licence, observation/forecast/scenario/planning/synthetic class, location, issue/valid/expiry time, units/datum, quality and coverage; distinguish NoData, Unknown, modeled zero and not applicable.

findings.summary: First-72-hour hazard and service trajectories lack confirmed actions, resources and blockers.
findings.evidence: Pluvial clears while burden grows 63,219→135,655; wildfire smoke clears while burden grows 22,643→65,384; compound depth persists while burden grows 187,285→762,012. E03/E06 define conditional roles and handover, not completed local actions.

findings.summary: Exact map values can visually outrank partial registers, official scenarios and Unknown local state.
